sanskrit: atrādyāho nivatsyāmaḥ kṣapāṃ bharatasattama dvāram etad dhi kaunteya kurukṣetrasya bhārata
english: Here, O best of the Bharatas, we shall spend the night today — for this, O son of Kuntī, is the gateway to Kurukṣetra, O Bharata.

sanskrit: atraiva nāhuṣo rājā rājan kratubhir iṣṭavān yayātir bahuratnāḍhyair yatrendro mudam abhyagāt
english: Here indeed, O king, King Yayāti, son of Nahuṣa, performed sacrifices with many jewel-rich rites, at which even Indra was gladdened.

sanskrit: etat plakṣāvataraṇaṃ yamunātīrtham ucyate etad vai nākapṛṣṭhasya dvāram āhur manīṣiṇaḥ
english: This is called Plakṣāvaraṇa, the sacred ford of the Yamunā; the wise declare this to be the gateway to the vault of heaven.

sanskrit: atra sārasvatair yajñair ījānāḥ paramarṣayaḥ yūpolūkhalinas tāta gacchanty avabhṛthāplavam
english: Here, O dear one, the great sages who have performed Sārasvata sacrifices, bearing the sacrificial post and the mortar, proceed to the final ablution bath.

sanskrit: atraiva bharato rājā medhyam aśvam avāsṛjat asakṛt kṛṣṇasāraṅgaṃ dharmeṇāvāpya medinīm
english: Here indeed King Bharata released the consecrated horse — the dark-spotted steed — having won the earth by righteousness more than once.

sanskrit: atraiva puruṣavyāghra maruttaḥ satram uttamam āste devarṣimukhyena saṃvartenābhipālitaḥ
english: Here too, O tiger among men, Marutta performed the highest sacrifice session, presided over by Saṃvarta, foremost among divine sages.

sanskrit: atropaspṛśya rājendra sarvāṃl lokān prapaśyati pūyate duṣkṛtāc caiva samupaspṛśya bhārata
english: By touching the sacred waters here, O king of kings, one beholds all the worlds; and by duly touching them, O Bharata, one is purified of all evil deeds.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tatra sabhrātṛkaḥ snātvā stūyamāno maharṣibhiḥ lomaśaṃ pāṇḍavaśreṣṭha idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: There, having bathed along with his brothers and being praised by the great sages, the foremost of the Pāṇḍavas spoke these words to Lomaśa.

sanskrit: sarvāṃl lokān prapaśyāmi tapasā satyavikrama ihasthaḥ pāṇḍavaśreṣṭhaṃ paśyāmi śvetavāhanam
english: "I behold all the worlds by the power of austerity, O you whose valor is truth; standing here I see the foremost of Pāṇḍavas, the white-horsed Arjuna."

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca evam etan mahābāho paśyanti paramarṣayaḥ sarasvatīm imāṃ puṇyāṃ paśyaikaśaraṇāvṛtām
english: Lomaśa said: Even so, O mighty-armed one, the great sages see this; behold this holy Sarasvatī, adorned with Ekaśaraṇa.

sanskrit: yatra snātvā naraśreṣṭha dhūtapāpmā bhaviṣyati iha sārasvatair yajñair iṣṭavantaḥ surarṣayaḥ ṛṣayaś caiva kaunteya tathā rājarṣayo 'pi ca
english: Bathing here, O best of men, one becomes cleansed of sin; here the divine sages, the sages, O son of Kuntī, and the royal sages as well, have worshipped with Sārasvata sacrifices.

sanskrit: vedī prajāpater eṣā samantāt pañcayojanā kuror vai yajñaśīlasya kṣetram etan mahātmanaḥ
english: This is the altar of Prajāpati, extending five yojanas on all sides — this is the sacred field of Kuru the great soul, devoted to sacrifice.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca iha martyās tapas taptvā svargaṃ gacchanti bhārata martukāmā narā rājann ihāyānti sahasraśaḥ
english: Lomaśa said: Here, O Bharata, mortals go to heaven by performing austerities; men desiring death, O king, come here by the thousands.

sanskrit: evam āśīḥ prayuktā hi dakṣeṇa yajatā purā iha ye vai mariṣyanti te vai svargajito narāḥ
english: For such was the blessing pronounced long ago by Dakṣa when he sacrificed — those who die here are truly men who have conquered heaven.

sanskrit: eṣā sarasvatī puṇyā divyā coghavatī nadī etad vinaśanaṃ nāma sarasvatyā viśāṃ pate
english: This is the holy, divine Sarasvatī, the river of plentiful waters; and this, O lord of the people, is called Vinaśana, the disappearance of the Sarasvatī.

sanskrit: dvāraṃ niṣādarāṣṭrasya yeṣāṃ dveṣāt sarasvatī praviṣṭā pṛthivīṃ vīra mā niṣādā hi māṃ viduḥ
english: This is the gateway to the realm of the Niṣādas, out of hatred for whom the Sarasvatī entered the earth — for the river said, "May the Niṣādas not know me."

sanskrit: eṣa vai camasodbhedo yatra dṛśyā sarasvatī yatrainām abhyavartanta divyāḥ puṇyāḥ samudragāḥ
english: This is Camasodbheda, where the Sarasvatī becomes visible again, where the divine, holy rivers flowing to the sea converged upon her.

sanskrit: etat sindhor mahat tīrthaṃ yatrāgastyam ariṃdama lopāmudrā samāgamya bhartāram avṛṇīta vai
english: This is the great sacred ford of the Sindhu where Lopāmudrā, O subduer of foes, met and chose Agastya as her husband.

sanskrit: etat prabhāsate tīrthaṃ prabhāsaṃ bhāskaradyute indrasya dayitaṃ puṇyaṃ pavitraṃ pāpanāśanam
english: This is the sacred ford called Prabhāsa, O you who shine like the sun — the beloved holy shrine of Indra, pure and destroying sin.

sanskrit: etad viṣṇupadaṃ nāma dṛśyate tīrtham uttamam eṣā ramyā vipāśā ca nadī paramapāvanī
english: Here is seen the excellent sacred ford named Viṣṇupada; and this is the lovely river Vipāśā, supremely purifying.

sanskrit: atraiva putraśokena vasiṣṭho bhagavān ṛṣiḥ baddhvātmānaṃ nipatito vipāśaḥ punar utthitaḥ
english: Here indeed the blessed sage Vasiṣṭha, overcome by grief for his son, bound himself and fell, but rose again unbound — hence the river Vipāśā, "the freed from bonds."

sanskrit: kāśmīramaṇḍalaṃ caitat sarvapuṇyam ariṃdama maharṣibhiś cādhyuṣitaṃ paśyedaṃ bhrātṛbhiḥ saha
english: This is the entirely holy region of Kāśmīra, O subduer of foes, inhabited by great sages — behold it together with your brothers.

sanskrit: atrottarāṇāṃ sarveṣām ṛṣīṇāṃ nāhuṣasya ca agneś cātraiva saṃvādaḥ kāśyapasya ca bhārata
english: Here took place the dialogue of all the northern sages, and of Nahuṣa, and of Agni, and of Kāśyapa as well, O Bharata.

sanskrit: etad dvāraṃ mahārāja mānasasya prakāśate varṣam asya girer madhye rāmeṇa śrīmatā kṛtam
english: This, O great king, is the gateway that leads to Mānasa lake; the land in the middle of this mountain was established by the glorious Rāma.

sanskrit: eṣa vātikaṣaṇḍo vai prakhyātaḥ satyavikramaḥ nābhyavartata yad dvāraṃ videhān uttaraṃ ca yaḥ
english: This is the renowned Vāṭikaṣaṇḍa grove — of true valor — the gateway which one who has not surpassed the Videhas and the northerners does not approach.

sanskrit: eṣa ujjānako nāma yavakrīr yatra śāntavān arundhatīsahāyaś ca vasiṣṭho bhagavān ṛṣiḥ
english: This is the place called Ujjānaka, where the peaceful Yavakrī dwelt, and where the blessed sage Vasiṣṭha resided together with Arundhatī.

sanskrit: hradaś ca kuśavān eṣa yatra padmaṃ kuśeśayam āśramaś caiva rukmiṇyā yatrāśāmyad akopanā
english: And this is the lake Kuśavān where the lotus blossoms; and here too is the hermitage where the wrathless Rukmiṇī was pacified.

sanskrit: samādhīnāṃ samāsas tu pāṇḍaveya śrutas tvayā taṃ drakṣyasi mahārāja bhṛgutuṅgaṃ mahāgirim
english: The confluence of the Samādhī rivers you have heard of, O son of Pāṇḍu — you shall behold it, O great king, and also the great mountain Bhṛgutuṅga.

sanskrit: jalāṃ copajalāṃ caiva yamunām abhito nadīm uśīnaro vai yatreṣṭvā vāsavād atyaricyata
english: And the rivers Jalā and Upajalā near the Yamunā — it was here that Uśīnara, having sacrificed, surpassed even Vāsava in merit.

sanskrit: tāṃ devasamitiṃ tasya vāsavaś ca viśāṃ pate abhyagacchata rājānaṃ jñātum agniś ca bhārata
english: To test that king at his divine assembly, both Vāsava and Agni, O lord of the people, came to King Uśīnara, O Bharata.

sanskrit: jijñāsamānau varadau mahātmānam uśīnaram indraḥ śyenaḥ kapoto 'gnir bhūtvā yajñe 'bhijagmatuḥ
english: Desiring to examine the great-souled Uśīnara, those two boon-givers — Indra taking the form of a hawk and Agni the form of a pigeon — came to his sacrifice.

sanskrit: ūruṃ rājñaḥ samāsādya kapotaḥ śyenajād bhayāt śaraṇārthī tadā rājan nililye bhayapīḍitaḥ
english: The pigeon, seeking refuge out of fear of the hawk, came to the king's thigh and pressed itself there, O king, tormented by fear and seeking shelter.

sanskrit: śyena uvāca dharmātmānaṃ tv āhur ekaṃ sarve rājan mahīkṣitaḥ sa vai dharmaviruddhaṃ tvaṃ kasmāt karma cikīrṣasi
english: The hawk said: All rulers of the earth proclaim you alone to be righteous of soul, O king — why then do you wish to perform an act contrary to dharma?

sanskrit: vihitaṃ bhakṣaṇaṃ rājan pīḍyamānasya me kṣudhā mā bhāṅkṣīr dharmalobhena dharmam utsṛṣṭavān asi
english: The eating of this prey is ordained for me, O king, as I am tormented by hunger — do not deprive me of it; by clinging to one form of dharma you have abandoned dharma altogether.

sanskrit: rājovāca saṃtrastarūpas trāṇārthī tvatto bhīto mahādvija matsakāśam anuprāptaḥ prāṇagṛdhnur ayaṃ dvijaḥ
english: The king said: This bird, terrified in form, seeking protection, frightened of you, O great twice-born, has come to me clinging to life.

sanskrit: evam abhyāgatasyeha kapotasyābhayārthinaḥ apradāne paro 'dharmaḥ kiṃ tvaṃ śyena prapaśyasi
english: For one who has thus come here seeking refuge — not granting protection to this pigeon would be the greatest adharma; what do you see in this, O hawk?

sanskrit: praspandamānaḥ saṃbhrāntaḥ kapotaḥ śyena lakṣyate matsakāśaṃ jīvitārthī tasya tyāgo vigarhitaḥ
english: This pigeon, trembling and distressed, is seen to be seeking life by coming to me, O hawk — to abandon him is blameworthy.

sanskrit: śyena uvāca āhārāt sarvabhūtāni saṃbhavanti mahīpate āhāreṇa vivardhante tena jīvanti jantavaḥ
english: The hawk said: All beings arise from food, O lord of the earth; through food they grow, and by it creatures live.

sanskrit: śakyate dustyaje 'py arthe cirarātrāya jīvitum na tu bhojanam utsṛjya śakyaṃ vartayituṃ ciram
english: One may live for a long time even after relinquishing what is hard to abandon; but giving up food, one cannot sustain life for long.

sanskrit: bhakṣyād vilopitasyādya mama prāṇā viśāṃ pate visṛjya kāyam eṣyanti panthānam apunarbhavam
english: Today, deprived of my prey, O lord of the people, my life-breath will leave this body and travel the path of no return.

sanskrit: pramṛte mayi dharmātman putradāraṃ naśiṣyati rakṣamāṇaḥ kapotaṃ tvaṃ bahūn prāṇān naśiṣyasi
english: If I die, O righteous one, my wife and children will perish; by protecting this pigeon you will destroy many lives.

sanskrit: dharmaṃ yo bādhate dharmo na sa dharmaḥ kudharma tat avirodhī tu yo dharmaḥ sa dharmaḥ satyavikrama
english: A dharma that obstructs another dharma is no dharma — that is pseudo-dharma; but dharma that does not conflict with another dharma — that, O you of true valor, is true dharma.

sanskrit: virodhiṣu mahīpāla niścitya gurulāghavam na bādhā vidyate yatra taṃ dharmaṃ samudācaret
english: When duties conflict, O lord of the earth, one should weigh what is greater and what is lesser, and practice whichever dharma causes no obstruction to others.

sanskrit: gurulāghavam ājñāya dharmādharmaviniścaye yato bhūyāṃs tato rājan kuru dharmaviniścayam
english: Having determined what is weightier and what is lighter in deciding between dharma and adharma, follow whichever is the greater, O king — thus make your determination of dharma.

sanskrit: rājovāca bahukalyāṇasaṃyuktaṃ bhāṣase vihagottama suparṇaḥ pakṣirāṭ kiṃ tvaṃ dharmajñaś cāsy asaṃśayam tathā hi dharmasaṃyuktaṃ bahu citraṃ prabhāṣase
english: The king said: You speak with much that is auspicious and good, O best of birds — are you Suparṇa, king of birds? You are certainly a knower of dharma, without doubt; for you speak much that is varied and full of dharma.

sanskrit: na te 'sty aviditaṃ kiṃ cid iti tvā lakṣayāmy aham śaraṇaiṣiṇaḥ parityāgaṃ kathaṃ sādhv iti manyase
english: I perceive that there is nothing unknown to you; yet how do you consider it right to abandon one who is seeking refuge?

sanskrit: āhārārthaṃ samārambhas tava cāyaṃ vihaṃgama śakyaś cāpy anyathā kartum āhāro 'py adhikas tvayā
english: Your purpose in this undertaking is to obtain food, O bird, and that may be accomplished otherwise — and indeed greater food may be obtained by you.

sanskrit: govṛṣo vā varāho vā mṛgo vā mahiṣo 'pi vā tvadartham adya kriyatāṃ yad vānyad abhikāṅkṣase
english: A bull, or a boar, or a deer, or even a buffalo — let whichever you desire be prepared for you today, or whatever else you may wish for.

sanskrit: śyena uvāca na varāhaṃ na cokṣāṇaṃ na mṛgān vividhāṃs tathā bhakṣayāmi mahārāja kim annādyena tena me
english: The hawk said: I do not eat boar, nor bull, nor various kinds of deer, O great king — what use is such food to me?

sanskrit: yas tu me daivavihito bhakṣaḥ kṣatriyapuṃgava tam utsṛja mahīpāla kapotam imam eva me
english: But the prey ordained for me by fate, O bull among kṣatriyas — release it to me, O lord of the earth; give me this very pigeon.

sanskrit: śyenāḥ kapotān khādanti sthitir eṣā sanātanī mā rājan mārgam ājñāya kadalīskandham āruha
english: Hawks eat pigeons — this is the eternal order of things; O king, knowing this path, do not climb a plantain trunk expecting fruit.

sanskrit: rājovāca rājyaṃ śibīnām ṛddhaṃ vai śādhi pakṣigaṇārcita yad vā kāmayase kiṃ cic chyena sarvaṃ dadāni te vinemaṃ pakṣiṇaṃ śyena śaraṇārthinam āgatam
english: The king said: O hawk, O honored by flocks of birds, rule the prosperous kingdom of the Śibis, or take whatever you desire — I will give you everything, but not this bird, O hawk, who has come seeking refuge.

sanskrit: yenemaṃ varjayethās tvaṃ karmaṇā pakṣisattama tad ācakṣva kariṣyāmi na hi dāsye kapotakam
english: Whatever act would make you relinquish this one, tell me, O best of birds — I will do it; for I will not give up this little pigeon.

sanskrit: śyena uvāca uśīnara kapote te yadi sneho narādhipa ātmano māṃsam utkṛtya kapotatulayā dhṛtam
english: The hawk said: O Uśīnara, O lord of men, if you have such love for this pigeon — then cut flesh from your own body and weigh it against the pigeon in the balance.

sanskrit: yadā samaṃ kapotena tava māṃsaṃ bhaven nṛpa tadā pradeyaṃ tan mahyaṃ sā me tuṣṭir bhaviṣyati
english: When your flesh equals the pigeon's weight in the balance, O king, then give that to me — that will be my satisfaction.

sanskrit: rājovāca anugraham imaṃ manye śyena yan mābhiyācase tasmāt te 'dya pradāsyāmi svamāṃsaṃ tulayā dhṛtam
english: The king said: I consider it a favor, O hawk, that you solicit me thus; therefore I will give you today my own flesh weighed in the balance.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca athotkṛtya svamāṃsaṃ tu rājā paramadharmavit tulayām āsa kaunteya kapotena sahābhibho
english: Lomaśa said: Then the king, a supreme knower of dharma, cut flesh from his body and placed it on the scale against the pigeon, O son of Kuntī, O illustrious one.

sanskrit: dhriyamāṇas tu tulayā kapoto vyatiricyate punaś cotkṛtya māṃsāni rājā prādād uśīnaraḥ
english: But the pigeon, when weighed in the balance, outweighed the flesh; so King Uśīnara cut more flesh and added it again.

sanskrit: na vidyate yadā māṃsaṃ kapotena samaṃ dhṛtam tata utkṛttamāṃso 'sāv āruroha svayaṃ tulām
english: When no more flesh could be found equal in weight to the pigeon, then that one, his flesh cut away, climbed upon the scale himself.

sanskrit: śyena uvāca indro 'ham asmi dharmajña kapoto havyavāḍ ayam jijñāsamānau dharme tvāṃ yajñavāṭam upāgatau
english: The hawk said: I am Indra, O knower of dharma, and this pigeon is Agni, the carrier of oblations — we two came to your sacrificial arena wishing to examine you in dharma.

sanskrit: yat te māṃsāni gātrebhya utkṛttāni viśāṃ pate eṣā te bhāsvarī kīrtir lokān abhibhaviṣyati
english: The flesh that has been cut from your limbs, O lord of the people — this your radiant fame will pervade all the worlds.

sanskrit: yāval loke manuṣyās tvāṃ kathayiṣyanti pārthiva tāvat kīrtiś ca lokāś ca sthāsyanti tava śāśvatāḥ
english: For as long as men in this world shall tell of you, O king, so long shall your fame and your worlds endure — eternal.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca tat pāṇḍaveya sadanaṃ rājñas tasya mahātmanaḥ paśyasvaitan mayā sārdhaṃ puṇyaṃ pāpapramocanam
english: Lomaśa said: Behold, O son of Pāṇḍu, the abode of that great-souled king — see it together with me; it is holy and releases one from sin.

sanskrit: atra vai satataṃ devā munayaś ca sanātanāḥ dṛśyante brāhmaṇai rājan puṇyavadbhir mahātmabhiḥ
english: Here the gods and the eternal sages are ever seen, O king, by virtuous brāhmaṇas of great souls.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca yaḥ kathyate mantravid agryabuddhir; auddālakiḥ śvetaketuḥ pṛthivyām tasyāśramaṃ paśya narendra puṇyaṃ; sadāphalair upapannaṃ mahījaiḥ
english: Lomaśa said: He who is celebrated on earth as a knower of sacred lore and of foremost intellect — Auddālaki Śvetaketu — behold his holy hermitage, O lord of men, adorned with ever-fruitful trees grown from the earth.

sanskrit: sākṣād atra śvetaketur dadarśa; sarasvatīṃ mānuṣadeharūpām vetsyāmi vāṇīm iti saṃpravṛttāṃ; sarasvatīṃ śvetaketur babhāṣe
english: Here Śvetaketu directly beheld Sarasvatī in human bodily form; "I shall master sacred speech" — so saying to Sarasvatī, Śvetaketu addressed her.

sanskrit: tasmin kāle brahmavidāṃ variṣṭhāv; āstāṃ tadā mātulabhāgineyau aṣṭāvakraś caiva kahoḍasūnur; auddālakiḥ śvetaketuś ca rājan
english: At that time, the two foremost knowers of Brahman — maternal uncle and nephew — were present: Aṣṭāvakra the son of Kahoḍa, and Auddālaki Śvetaketu, O king.

sanskrit: videharājasya mahīpates tau; viprāv ubhau mātulabhāgineyau praviśya yajñāyatanaṃ vivāde; bandiṃ nijagrāhatur aprameyam
english: Those two brāhmaṇas, uncle and nephew, entered the sacrificial arena of the king of Videha, that lord of the earth, and in debate subdued the immeasurable Bandin.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kathaṃprabhāvaḥ sa babhūva vipras; tathāyuktaṃ yo nijagrāha bandim aṣṭāvakraḥ kena cāsau babhūva; tat sarvaṃ me lomaśa śaṃsa tattvam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: What was the power of that brāhmaṇa who thus subdued Bandin? How did Aṣṭāvakra come to be as he was? Tell me all of this truly, O Lomaśa.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca uddālakasya niyataḥ śiṣya eko; nāmnā kahoḍeti babhūva rājan śuśrūṣur ācāryavaśānuvartī; dīrghaṃ kālaṃ so 'dhyayanaṃ cakāra
english: Lomaśa said: There was one devoted disciple of Uddālaka, named Kahoḍa, O king, who served his teacher obediently and studied for a long time.

sanskrit: taṃ vai viprāḥ paryabhavaṃś ca śiṣyās; taṃ ca jñātvā viprakāraṃ guruḥ saḥ tasmai prādāt sadya eva śrutaṃ ca; bhāryāṃ ca vai duhitaraṃ svāṃ sujātām
english: Yet the brāhmaṇa students surpassed him in learning; and knowing this slight, his teacher at once gave him both sacred knowledge and his own beautiful daughter Sujātā as wife.

sanskrit: tasyā garbhaḥ samabhavad agnikalpaḥ; so 'dhīyānaṃ pitaram athābhyuvāca sarvāṃ rātrim adhyayanaṃ karoṣi; nedaṃ pitaḥ samyag ivopavartate
english: A child like fire formed in her womb; while still in the womb that child then spoke to its father who was studying: "All night long you study — but, Father, this does not seem to me to be going rightly."

sanskrit: upālabdhaḥ śiṣyamadhye maharṣiḥ; sa taṃ kopād udarasthaṃ śaśāpa yasmāt kukṣau vartamāno bravīṣi; tasmād vakro bhavitāsy aṣṭakṛtvaḥ
english: Reproached thus in the midst of his students, the great sage cursed that child in his womb in anger: "Because you speak while still in the belly, therefore you shall be crooked in eight places."

sanskrit: sa vai tathā vakra evābhyajāyad; aṣṭāvakraḥ prathito vai maharṣiḥ tasyāsīd vai mātulaḥ śvetaketuḥ; sa tena tulyo vayasā babhūva
english: And so he was born crooked — the great sage renowned as Aṣṭāvakra, "crooked in eight places." His maternal uncle was Śvetaketu, who was equal to him in age.

sanskrit: saṃpīḍyamānā tu tadā sujātā; vivardhamānena sutena kukṣau uvāca bhartāram idaṃ rahogatā; prasādya hīnaṃ vasunā dhanārthinī
english: But Sujātā, then oppressed by the growing child in her womb and in need of wealth, took her husband aside in private, and having conciliated him, she said to him in his poverty.

sanskrit: kathaṃ kariṣyāmy adhanā maharṣe; māsaś cāyaṃ daśamo vartate me na cāsti te vasu kiṃ cit prajātā; yenāham etām āpadaṃ nistareyam
english: "What shall I do without wealth, O great sage? This is my tenth month; you have not a single possession, O you who are to be a father — with which I might cross this difficulty."

sanskrit: uktas tv evaṃ bhāryayā vai kahoḍo; vittasyārthe janakam athābhyagacchat sa vai tadā vādavidā nigṛhya; nimajjito bandinehāpsu vipraḥ
english: Thus addressed by his wife, Kahoḍa went to Janaka for wealth; but there he was subdued by Bandin, skilled in debate, and the brāhmaṇa was drowned in the waters.

sanskrit: uddālakas taṃ tu tadā niśamya; sūtena vāde 'psu tathā nimajjitam uvāca tāṃ tatra tataḥ sujātām; aṣṭāvakre gūhitavyo 'yam arthaḥ
english: Then Uddālaka, hearing that he had been drowned in the water after being vanquished in debate by the sūta, said to Sujātā there and then: "This matter must be concealed from Aṣṭāvakra."

sanskrit: rarakṣa sā cāpy ati taṃ sumantraṃ; jāto 'py evaṃ na sa śuśrāva vipraḥ uddālakaṃ pitṛvac cāpi mene; aṣṭāvakro bhrātṛvac chvetaketum
english: She guarded that secret exceedingly well; even after his birth, the brāhmaṇa [Aṣṭāvakra] did not come to know of it; and Aṣṭāvakra regarded Uddālaka as a father and Śvetaketu as a brother.

sanskrit: tato varṣe dvādaśe śvetaketur; aṣṭāvakraṃ pitur aṅke nisannam apākarṣad gṛhya pāṇau rudantaṃ; nāyaṃ tavāṅkaḥ pitur ity uktavāṃś ca
english: Then in the twelfth year, Śvetaketu pulled Aṣṭāvakra away by the hand as he sat weeping on his father's lap, and said to him: "This is not your father's lap."
